# rt

> The runtime truck: memory, vectors, strings, maps, files, processes, time and terminals.

[source](../../registry/rt.pkg) · truck

Library packages written in Packenger itself, on top of `std` and system
calls. They are what `pkc`, the self-hosted compiler, is built on.

```
use std
use rt

let words = vec_new()
let counts = map_new()
let ok = false
let text = io_read_file("notes.txt", &ok)
...
io_flush()
```

| package | provides |
|---|---|
| `rt/mem` | `mem_alloc`, `mem_copy`, `mem_set`, `mem_eq`, `mem_add`, `rt_panic` |
| `rt/vec` | `Vec`: growable arrays of words |
| `rt/str` | string functions and the `StrBuf` builder |
| `rt/map` | `Map`: string keys to words, in insertion order |
| `rt/io` | files, buffered stdout, stderr |
| `rt/os` | environment, `PATH` lookup, running programs, exit |
| `rt/time` | monotonic clock and duration text |
| `rt/term` | terminal detection and colors |
| `rt/test` | checks for tests written in Packenger |

Every name is prefixed with its package (`vec_push`, `str_find`), since
libraries share one namespace with the program. Containers hold one-word
values; convert pointers and strings with `as`. Memory is never freed.
Each package's tests are in [tests/rt](../../tests/rt).

## Packages

| package | summary |
|---|---|
| [rt/mem](rt/mem.md) | Raw memory: an allocator on mmap, plus copy, fill, compare and pointer arithmetic. |
| [rt/vec](rt/vec.md) | Growable arrays of 64-bit words (ints, or pointers and strings with as). |
| [rt/str](rt/str.md) | Strings: slicing, searching, joining, numbers, and a string builder. |
| [rt/map](rt/map.md) | Hash map from strings to 64-bit words, iterated in insertion order. |
| [rt/io](rt/io.md) | Files and output: whole-file reads and writes, buffered stdout, stderr. |
| [rt/os](rt/os.md) | The process: environment variables, finding and running programs, exiting. |
| [rt/time](rt/time.md) | Time: a monotonic clock in nanoseconds, and durations as text. |
| [rt/term](rt/term.md) | Terminals: detecting one, and ANSI colors that respect NO_COLOR. |
| [rt/test](rt/test.md) | A tiny test library: checks that print FAIL lines, and a final PASS or FAILED. |
